Welcome to Blume and our Terms of Use (the “Agreement”).

By accessing or using the website, or blog (collectively, the “Site”) provided by Blume, including www.meetblume.com, you agree to be bound be the terms and conditions in this Agreement and other terms incorporated herein by reference. This Agreement applies to all users of the Site.

The website www.meetblume.com is a subscription based marketplace platform for services performed by its users. The following terms and conditions are the T

Cancellation Policy
Some items in our store may be offered to you as a subscription, a pre-order or try before you buy. This cancellation policy lays out how you can change or cancel these kinds of purchases.

Subscriptions
When you purchase a subscription you'll receive repeat deliveries. These are based on the subscription duration and frequency that you select.
Your payment details will be stored securely and you'll be charged for each of these deliveries, unless you choose to pay in advance.
Orders will ship within 1-3 business days.

We want you to love what you receive but we totally understand if you need a refund. Email us at customer@example.test within 30 days of your order and we’ll help you process a return. Please note that our pads and tampons are final sale.

This Privacy Policy (this "Policy") describes the privacy practices of Blume with respect to information collected when you sign up for, use, access or otherwise interact with www.meetblume.com (the "Site") and any online services and products of Blume, including mobile applications and websites or applications operated by Blume and connected products and services (collectively, including the Sites, the "Services") that reference this Policy, and how we use and share that information. evidenceLineItems.label: AVS/CVV verification
evidenceLineItems.reason: Held on file. Using it would weaken your case, so it is left out.

internalSignals.label: Card security check partially passed
internalSignals.reason: The address did not match the card issuer's records, but the card's security code did (AVS N, CVV M). The matching security code is kept as an internal record — it is not cited in the dispute response, because a security-code match is not an address match.

internalSignals.label: Card is registered to a different name than the buyer
internalSignals.reason: The payment card is registered to "Customer 4" but the order was placed by "Customer 1". This is a common stolen-card pattern — review before submitting. Used internally for assessment; not added to the bank-facing argument.

evidenceLineItems.label: 3-D Secure authentication, if available
evidenceLineItems.reason: The payment receipt does not include 3-D Secure authentication data for this transaction.

evidenceLineItems.label: Shopify fraud screening
evidenceLineItems.reason: Not verified, so it is not used in the defence.

evidenceLineItems.label: Order confirmation
evidenceLineItems.reason: Confirms order details, but does not prove the customer authorized the transaction.

internalSignals.label: Billing and shipping addresses on the order agree
internalSignals.reason: The billing and shipping addresses you hold for this order have the same city and country. This is an internal note about your own order record, not evidence: it is not a check by the cardholder's bank, so it is never scored and never included in the dispute response. Address verification comes from the issuer's AVS result on the payment row.

evidenceLineItems.label: IP location vs billing country
evidenceLineItems.reason: The order IP geolocated to the same country as the billing and shipping address, with no VPN, proxy, or datacenter signals. Cited as supporting context — consistent with a cardholder-originated transaction.

evidenceLineItems.label: Customer correspondence from Shopify timeline/notes
evidenceLineItems.reason: No customer correspondence is on file for this order. Upload a transcript from your helpdesk to add one.

evidenceLineItems.label: Shipping tracking
evidenceLineItems.reason: The carrier confirmed delivery with a timestamp — strong support that the order arrived.

evidenceLineItems.label: activity_log
evidenceLineItems.reason: Included in the defence package as context, not as decisive proof.

evidenceLineItems.label: shipping_policy
evidenceLineItems.reason: Held on file. It does not support this type of claim, so the letter does not rely on it.

evidenceLineItems.label: refund_policy
evidenceLineItems.reason: Held on file. It does not support this type of claim, so the letter does not rely on it.

evidenceLineItems.label: cancellation_policy
evidenceLineItems.reason: Held on file. It does not support this type of claim, so the letter does not rely on it.

toWin: Customer behavior is consistent with legitimate purchase
caseTypeInfo.issuerClaim: Customer claims the transaction was not authorized

value.bankLocationSummary: The order was placed from an IP address geolocating to the same country as the order's shipping destination, with no VPN, proxy or datacenter signals.

chronologyArgument.text: The order was placed via the web channel and an order record was created at that time. The carrier subsequently confirmed delivery on 9 July 2026 (TechSHIP, tracking TRK000001). Following delivery, no return or reversal was initiated by the cardholder. The available records indicate a sequential progression from order placement through to carrier-confirmed delivery, with no post-delivery contact or return request on file.

conclusion.text: The available evidence supports the merchant's position in response to this unauthorized transaction claim. The carrier confirmed delivery on 9 July 2026 (TechSHIP, tracking TRK000001), no return has been initiated, and the order IP geolocation is consistent with a cardholder-placed order. The submitted records, taken together, are consistent with a cardholder-authorized transaction under Mastercard reason code 4837, and the merchant respectfully requests that the dispute be resolved in its favour.

executiveSummary.text: The available records support the merchant's position that this transaction was consistent with a cardholder-authorized purchase. The carrier confirmed delivery on 9 July 2026 (TechSHIP, tracking TRK000001), and no return has been initiated. The available evidence is consistent with a cardholder-initiated transaction under Mastercard reason code 4837.

fulfillmentArgument.text: The carrier confirmed delivery on 9 July 2026 (TechSHIP, tracking TRK000001). The available records indicate that the shipment was marked as delivered by the carrier at 15:35 UTC on that date. Following this delivery confirmation, no return was initiated and no claim of non-receipt was raised prior to the dispute.

omittedSections.reason: No approved customer communication facts are present in approvedFacts.
Policy disclosure is not relevant to an unauthorized-transaction claim. The argument hinges on cardholder authentication signals, not the merchant's published terms.
No manual evidence was submitted for this case.

paymentAuthenticationArgument.text: The available records indicate that the transaction was processed on the Mastercard network. The order IP address geolocated to the same country as the order's shipping destination, with no VPN, proxy, or datacenter signals — consistent with a cardholder placing the order from their usual location. Taken together, the available evidence is consistent with a cardholder-initiated transaction and supports the conclusion that the transaction was authorized by the account holder.

transactionOverviewArgument.text: The available records indicate that this order was placed via the web channel and subsequently fulfilled. The transaction was processed on the Mastercard network. The submitted records are consistent with a standard customer-initiated purchase, and no indicators of account compromise or irregular order behaviour are present in the order record.
